milestone: M1.6 — channel-major layout transforms (TRACE-inspired) under the BF3 single-standard-deflate-stream constraint
verdict_note: RED per the PRE-REGISTERED worst-captured-model rule (bf16 alpha*=0.697 > 0.695; fp8_e5m2 alpha*=0.724 > 0.72 — both set by gpt2). The models DISAGREE beyond the 0.01 agreement bound (bf16 spread 0.025, e5m2 spread 0.020): on Qwen2.5-7B — the modern, deployment-representative architecture — the mechanism delivers a REAL gain (bf16 0.708->0.671, fp8_e5m2 0.732->0.704, the first fp8 transform win in this project). The architecture-dependence is itself the finding: per-channel scale structure is strong in GQA/RoPE/RMSNorm-era KV and weak in gpt2. Claimable multi-model numbers remain M1.5's (bf16 0.705-0.708, e5m2 0.731-0.732). THIRD-MODEL RESOLUTION (same day, pre-registered rule): Llama-3.1-8B confirms gpt2 is the architecture outlier for fp8_e5m2 (0.699, within 0.005 of Qwen's 0.704) -> RE-REGISTERED narrow claim: fp8_e5m2 chan YELLOW at alpha*=0.704 scoped to modern-architecture (GQA/RoPE) KV. bf16 lands in the pre-registered in-between zone (0.690: clears YELLOW individually but 0.019 from Qwen > 0.01 agreement bound) -> NO bf16 re-registration; both modern models clearing 0.695 individually is reported as an observation only.

third_model_extension.rule: pre-registered in EVALUATION_CONTRACT_M1.6.md BEFORE the capture ran (agreement bound 0.01 vs Qwen per dtype; re-register scoped to modern-arch KV iff agree AND worst-of-modern clears original thresholds)
third_model_extension.model: NousResearch/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B (ungated mirror of meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B; 32 layers, 8 KV heads, head_dim 128)

bf16.resolution: in-between zone -> NO re-registration (rule is strict; both clear YELLOW individually — observation only)

third_model_extension.gpt2_status: confirmed architecture outlier for e5m2; for bf16 the three models form a gradient (gpt2 0.697 > llama 0.690 > qwen 0.671) rather than a clean modern/legacy split

criteria.rule: best concat alpha, medians on captured KV, worst model across gpt2 + Qwen2.5-7B; synthetic never drives the verdict

alpha_concat_medians._doc: alpha = compressed/original, deflate(zlib L6) on the WHOLE transformed buffer as ONE stream (BF3-decodable, M2-proven). raw = untransformed. byte_transpose = M1.5 baseline.

synthetic_7b._doc: mechanism control: standard-normal KV has NO per-channel scale structure, so chan_bt == byte_transpose here (0.702=0.702) — confirms the captured gains are real structure, not a harness artifact.

per_tensor_type_medians_chan_best._doc: prefill only (gpt2 decode spans < 256KB chunk minimum). bf16 = chan_bt, fp8_e5m2 = chan.

transform_throughput_mbps_median._doc: single-thread numpy on the box; all permutation/prefix-sum class (DPU-ARM/FPGA far faster)

findings: Channel-major reordering + byte-transpose (chan_bt) is the first transform to beat M1.5's byte_transpose on real KV — but only decisively on the modern model (Qwen2.5-7B bf16 0.671 vs 0.708; gpt2 only 0.697 vs 0.705).
chan is the FIRST transform that helps fp8 at all (e5m2: qwen 0.732->0.704, gpt2 0.731->0.724); M1.5's bit-split had only hurt it. 1-byte values can't be byte-transposed, but they CAN be reordered.

Delta coding HURTS on top of chan_bt for gpt2 (0.719 vs 0.697) and helps nothing enough elsewhere (qwen 0.692 vs 0.671): within-channel exponent sequences are not smooth enough for delta to beat deflate's own LZ matching.
fp8_e4m3 improves slightly (0.826-0.832) but remains far outside the 0.75 gate.

TRACE's remaining gap is priced: of TRACE's bf16 0.799->~0.53 total win, the single-deflate-stream-portable share is 0.799->0.671 (Qwen) / ->0.690 (Llama) / ->0.697 (gpt2); the rest (~0.14-0.17 alpha) requires their custom bit-plane entropy silicon.
All 4068 rows bit-exact (transform∘invert AND deflate roundtrip); 612 captured + 3456 synthetic.

Third model (Llama-3.1-8B): e5m2 chan 0.730->0.699 lands within 0.005 of Qwen -> gpt2 confirmed as the e5m2 architecture outlier; RE-REGISTERED narrow claim fp8_e5m2 YELLOW alpha*=0.704 on modern-arch KV. bf16 forms a gradient (0.697/0.690/0.671) not a clean split -> no bf16 re-registration per the strict pre-registered agreement bound.
Llama K compresses better than V (bf16 0.685/0.696, e5m2 0.692/0.705) — opposite of gpt2 (V better); per-tensor structure is itself architecture-dependent.
